mapping_basis: Actual source post and per-photo captions, individually viewed images001-014 and primary ten-stanza text. Five different photographs map to S002.

references.caption_excerpt: #1 Devas and Asuras churned the milk ocean with the help of the Lord. First, Kalakoota poison emerged which was swallowed by Lord Shiva with great mercy for the mankind.

images.actual_visual_observation: 001 close Shiva poison-drinking icon; no literal full-body shore scene.

references.caption_excerpt: #2 Next came, the divine cow - Kamadhenu the beautiful horse - Uchchaishravas the great elephant - Iravatham Kalpaka vrusha Apsaras came too. All of them were gifted to Gods & sages.

images.actual_visual_observation: 002 human-faced winged cow churning composite;003 seven-headed horse;004 four-tusked elephant;005 wish-tree;006 winged dancer composite. Use subject cues, not copied rendering/hybrids/UI.

references.caption_excerpt: #3 As the ocean was churned further, Goddess Mahalakshmi appeared. Her magical form attracted everyone.

images.actual_visual_observation: 007 four-armed general Lakshmi emergence icon; narrative composition follows existing two-arm Lakshmi contract.

references.caption_excerpt: #4 The Goddess who had set her heart on Bhagwan was given a bejewelled throne by Indra. With the objects which everyone had brought, the sages consecrated her and sang Vedas.

images.actual_visual_observation: 008 floating Lakshmi and deva crowd, not a literal Indra seat/consecration action. Verse/caption ground action.

references.caption_excerpt: #5 The divine sages did abhishekam to Goddess Lakshmi with holy Ganga water. Goddess Mahalakshmi decked with studded earrings, yellow garment and necklaces appeared enchanting.

images.actual_visual_observation: 009 static four-arm yellow Lakshmi icon, not literal water ritual. Verse/caption ground bathing and yellow costume.

references.caption_excerpt: #6 Goddess Mahalakshmi with extreme devotion approached to Bhagwan with the divine garland in her hand.

images.actual_visual_observation: 010 garland approach icon; preserve action, use existing narrative two-arm Lakshmi identity.

references.caption_excerpt: #7 Goddess Lakshmi realised that all other Gods as Shiva Brahmaa and others though endowed with virtues, were not free from all defects. Bhagwan Vishnu who was perfect in every way, she put the divine garland on Bhagwan.

images.actual_visual_observation: 011 Vishnu/Lakshmi garlanding with other gods; two central figures selected, mentioned Shiva/Brahma need not physically join.

references.caption_excerpt: #8 Bhagwan readily accepted Goddess Mahalakshmi on Bhagwan’s bosom giving her due respect and honor as she was solely devoted. Her compassionate glances brought prosperity to the whole world.

images.actual_visual_observation: 012 Lakshmi in front of Vishnu with elephants; verse honour/bosom symbolism becomes two distinct seated figures, no duplicate goddess.

references.caption_excerpt: #9 Next the Goddess Varuni, the deity for wine came, who was intoxicating in appearence and is a source of all sins. Bhagwan presented her to the asuras as they are the seat of ignorance.

images.actual_visual_observation: 013 Varuni with bowl; modest scene adaptation and asura context from verse/caption.

references.caption_excerpt: #10 Dhanvanthri, a beautiful form of Lord, finally appeared from the ocean carrying the divine nectar in his hands. Bhattathiri praises Bhagwan for having made world get such priceless gifts by his mercy and requests that he cure him of his ailments.

images.actual_visual_observation: 014 generic eight-armed divine/medical icon, not literal ocean emergence. Verse/caption ground Dhanvantari with nectar pot carried in two hands.
